precepts.text: Now some of you are saying, she is all jacked up though. Here is the surprise: a wicked woman is given as a portion to a wicked man, but a godly woman is given to him that feareth the Lord. So ask yourself, why was she given to me? What am I not reflecting on, how am I not being real with myself, to understand why I am in the situation I am in? You see all of her flaws and you look at yourself like you never did anything wrong.
precepts.point: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun. Which he hath given thee: brothers, the Lord gave her to you. That sister was created for you. This is your portion all the days of your life.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.why:
“Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun”. Brothers, who gave her to you? The Lord did. Look at your wife: that sister was created for you. “for that is thy portion in this life”.

Now some of you are saying, God did that? She all jacked up, though. Here is another surprise: “A wicked woman is given as a portion to a wicked man: but a godly woman is given to him that feareth the Lord.” Nobody here wrote the Bible. That is what the scripture says.

So ask yourself, why is she jacked up? Because you're jacked up; she was created just for you. Brothers see all of her flaws, all of her issues, every problem she has, and look at themselves like they never did anything wrong. Ask yourself: why was she given to me? What am I doing, what am I not reflecting on, how am I not being real with myself, to understand why I am in the situation I am in?

precepts.text: A good wife is a good portion, which shall be given in the portion of them that fear the Lord. If you are not serious about this walk, how can you expect a righteous woman? Everybody says I want that virtuous woman, but you have been in sin the whole time you have been in this truth and you want the Proverbs 31. No sir; that is not your portion. It goes according to where your faith is at. Now it is not always the case; sometimes a husband is righteous and he is trying to correct his wife and get her right.
precepts.point: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun. Which he hath given thee: brothers, the Lord gave her to you. That sister was created for you. This is your portion all the days of your life.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.why:
“A good wife is a good portion, which shall be given in the portion of them that fear the Lord.” A good wife is given to him that deserves a good wife: to them that fear the Lord. She is the portion Solomon spoke of in Ecclesiastes 9:9.

So think about this, brothers. If you are not serious about this walk in this truth, not serious about what you are supposed to be doing, how could you expect a righteous woman? Everybody says, I want that virtuous woman. But you nasty. You have been committing adultery since you have been in the truth, and you want the Proverbs 31? No, sir. You get the scum, the bottom of the barrel. Why? Because of where your faith is at.

Now, let's be real: it is not always the case. Sisters will say, well, if I messed up, that means you messed up. No. Sometimes a husband is trying to get you right. Sometimes he is trying to correct you, trying to show you what he wants so that you can be who he wants you to be. It ain't always him.

precepts.text: As the sun when it ariseth in the high heaven, so is the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of her house. The way you set it up, the way you do things, that is your beauty. And for you brothers whose wives only clean for presentation when company comes: you have to order your house and demand what the desire of your home is.
precepts.point: Be honest, sisters: when it comes to the ordering of the house, most husbands let you do what you want with the drapes, the pots, the design. Most men are not fighting you over the couch set. So stop acting like submission is slavery; most of that is exaggeration.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.why:
“As the sun when it ariseth in the high heaven; so is the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of her house.” The way she sets it up and the way she does things: that is her beauty.

Ephesians 5 says “as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.” Submitting “as unto the Lord” means listening to your husband as you would to Christ, and assisting him in what he wants. It is the house of the husband, the house of Abiel, not the house of Abiel and his wife. When you understand whose house it is, you understand whose desires set what the house is supposed to be. If he wants a sound home, give him a sound home; if he wants a clean house, give him a clean house. The confusion comes when a sister thinks her aspirations supersede his. We are on the same team, but somebody is the CEO of the team making the decisions for the franchise.

Be honest, sisters: in the ordering of the house, most husbands let you do pretty much what you want. I don’t give a damn about them pots. The drapes, the knives and forks, the couch set: most men are not tripping over that. As long as he comes home to good food and a clean house, however she got there is fine. So stop acting like submission is straight slavery; most of that is exaggeration. If she wants to lift the carpet and vacuum the cushion every morning, that is her ordering, and that is her beauty.

For the brothers whose wives do not want to clean except when company comes over, cleaning for presentation: you have to order your house. Tell her this is not the desire of your home, this is what needs to be done, and demand it. For the brothers with neat freaks, that is a blessing; sometimes you have to calm them down.

This is also what Titus 2 means by “keepers at home”: a good wife in the ordering of her house, not idle, not a busybody in everybody else’s house, taking care of home.

precepts.text: My son, keep the flower of thine age sound, and give not thy strength to strangers: do not give your strength to other nations, or wicked women. When thou hast gotten a fruitful possession through all the field, sow it with thine own seed: sow with thine own race; trusting in the goodness of thy stock. So thy race which thou leavest shall be magnified, having the confidence of their good descent. You did not know the word race was in the Bible in terms of your nationality. This is what your sons and daughters have to know, instead of running around giving their seed to any old thing out there in the world.
precepts.point: A lot of you black women don't understand this.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
Babylon chose children of Israel “in whom was no blemish”, and the white man's own books say the stock landed in America was the soundest and strongest. A lot of our women don't understand this. “My son, keep the flower of thine age sound; and give not thy strength to strangers.” Don't give your strength to other nations, or to wicked women.

“When thou hast gotten a fruitful possession through all the field, sow it with thine own seed”: sow with thine own race. “trusting in the goodness of thy stock.” That's some good stock right there, and some of you are ashamed of it.

“So thy race which thou leavest shall be magnified, having the confidence of their good descent.” You didn't know the word race was in the Bible, in terms of ethnicity, in terms of your nationality. This is what your sons and daughters have to know, instead of running around giving their seed to any old thing out there in the world.

And don't hold your breath for reparations. Esau is not stupid. After slavery we had no reparations and still built great, advanced societies without white folks, and they came up with a reason to drop dynamite on us and destroy them, even Seneca Village in Central Park. Trust in the goodness of your stock: we can build without them.

precepts.text: There be three things that mine heart feareth: the slander of a city, the gathering together of an unruly multitude, and a false accusation: all these are worse than death. Simon did all three: he slandered the city, gathered the Greeks together to get the money from Jerusalem, and falsely accused Onias.
precepts.point: But when their hatred went so far, that by one of Simon's faction murders were committed: Simon hated Onias so much he had one of his men kill one of Onias's priests. That is why I say it is never just one thing; it is a domino effect of sins.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.why:
“There be three things that mine heart feareth; and for the fourth I was sore afraid: the slander of a city, the gathering together of an unruly multitude, and a false accusation: all these are worse than death.”

Simon did all three. The slander of a city: God does not like that thing, and Simon slandered the city. The gathering together of an unruly multitude: Simon had all the Greeks gather together to try to get the money from Jerusalem. And a false accusation: he accused Onias of doing this to Heliodorus. God said all these are worse than death.

Then think about this: don’t tell me what they say about me, tell me why they feel so comfortable telling you. In every school there is that one brother or sister that all the murmurers draw to, and they tell them all the things they don’t like about people. Why do they draw to you? You obviously did not have our back, because they are slandering and they feel so comfortable saying evil to you.

A deacon once pointed out a sister in red shoes with high heels and called her a hoe because of the shoes. The Bishop called Deacon Asaf, Deacon Malachi and the others over and asked them if she was; they said no. And he blew that brother’s spot up in front of them. You cannot come to me with evil. We must train ourselves to hate evil.

precepts.text: Give not thy strength to strangers; when thou hast gotten a fruitful possession through all the field, sow it with thine own seed, trusting in the goodness of thy stock, so shall thy race which thou leavest be magnified, having the confidence of their good descent; Israel has every color and feature, so there is no reason to step out.
precepts.point: Put your seed in the womb that belongs to you; a child of mixed seed grows up confused and shunned by both sides.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.why:
“My son, keep the flower of thine age sound; and give not thy strength to strangers.” Your strength is your seed, your legacy. Do not give it to strangers. It is the same thing God said in Malachi: we dealt treacherously against the wife of our youth by giving our seed to Moab and Ammon and Edom.

“When thou hast gotten a fruitful possession through all the field, sow it with thine own seed, trusting in the goodness of thy stock.” The fruitful possession is a woman. The field is the world: our people are found all throughout the world. Sow that fruitful possession with your own seed, and trust in the goodness of your stock, because your woman is your stock; she is your kind. Her womb is the soil that belongs to you, the housing for gods, which is why God made one, “That he might seek a godly seed.”

“So thy race which thou leavest shall be magnified, having the confidence of their good descent.” Your race, your legacy, shall be magnified. The children know that daddy and mommy come from royalty: daddy is Judah, mama is Ephraim, the same nation of people. That child does not grow up confused and lost. Mix your seed with the nations and the child grows up confused, not knowing what it is, and shunned by both sides; it is like forcing a triangle peg into a square hole.

Marry your own and stick with your own people. Israel is a multi-featured, multicolored people, an assortment of beautiful colors and features, so there is no reason to step out of your nation. Wanting to step out means you despise yourself. Even the rich Edomite understands that the womb of our women carries genetic perfection, dominant superior genes.

precepts.text: Blessed is the man that hath a virtuous wife, for the number of his days shall be doubled. A woman that honoureth her husband shall be judged wise of all, but she that dishonoureth him in her pride shall be counted ungodly of all. Honour is measured against what the scripture says. A man experiences love through respect, sincere and innate, not remembered and forced; if you have to remind yourself to respect your husband, you are not in submission.
precepts.point: He took her uprightly and they aged together mercifully, and with age comes beauty, love, and passion, not whimsical movie feelings. Stop chasing a feeling; get your mind like Tobit's. If even a majority of families moved in that spirit, how much stronger are we as a people for the time of trouble to come. Weddings are not done here for anyone who has not proved for three years.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

precepts.why:
“Blessed is the man that hath a virtuous wife, for the number of his days shall be double.” Virtuous deals with her character. Look how everything gets better in the marriage when the wife moves in that spirit; a virtuous wife brings peace. Tobias asked God that he and his wife might become aged together, and a virtuous wife doubles those days.

“A woman that honoureth her husband shall be judged wise of all; but she that dishonoureth him in her pride shall be counted ungodly of all.” She honors him by agreeing to follow what the Lord says; that's the honor. A woman that honors her husband equals wisdom for the woman. But not how you think: you measure it against the scripture and ask, am I fulfilling all of these things? Pride is what breaks the submission.

When Titus says to teach the women to love their husbands, we have taken it for years as surface emotions. A man experiences love through respect; that is the chief love language of a man. Why does he like being around the brothers so much? Because he's respected among his peers. If the wife reverences him, he'll feel the love, and everything else falls into place behind it.

And not forced respect. It has to come from a sincere place. If you have to remember and remind yourself to respect your husband, you're not in submission. If you really desire your husband and see him as he is, not through a warped worldly view, it will come out of you innately, and watch what will come out of him innately.

precepts.text: Teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, to be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed. If you are not applying this, sisters, you are blasphemous, and at the judgment seat, but my husband did this, will be answered, that was the man I gave you.
precepts.point: As the sun when it ariseth, so is the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of her house. As the clear light upon the holy candlestick, so is the beauty of the face in ripe age: apply this and your husband sees you beautiful past the gray hairs. As gold pillars upon sockets of silver, so are the fair feet with a constant heart. Beauty is functional, not sexualized; order equals beauty. Wives who neglect the home for other things are out of alignment with God's will; the home is the first priority, husband first, then children.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

precepts.why:
Sirach praises “A shamefaced and faithful woman”, “the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of her house”, and “the fair feet with a constant heart.” Beauty is functional, not sexualized. Order equals beauty, sisters. Wives who neglect the home for other things are out of order and out of alignment with God’s will. The home is your first priority above all things, starting with your husband and then your children.

Titus spells out that order: “That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed.” Keepers at home is what the ordering of her house goes into. It teaches them to love their husbands, and sums it up: obedient to their own husbands.

“That the word of God be not blasphemed.” If y’all are not applying this, sisters, you are blasphemous. And you think God will look past it, and at the judgment seat you will say, but my husband did this, my husband did that? He will say, that is blasphemy; that was the man I gave you.

If submission depends on how he treats you, it is not submission; it is manipulation. God told you to submit to your husband in everything, with no caveat. Proverbs 31 without genuine submission is decoration on a house with a weak foundation. Be soft, respectful and quiet; it is not your job to fix his issues but to make sure you are right.

This is the biblical model: complementary responsibilities. The woman’s list seems longer, but the man’s carries more weight. He is the head of the wife as Christ is head of the church, the savior of the body, accountable for you, the house, the children and the nation. Your accountability is only for yourself. Does that not deserve honor?

precepts.text: A virtuous woman rejoiceth her husband, and he shall fulfil the years of his life in peace. The Bible calls for peace in the marriage, not strife, variance, or division. Peace, not passion; the wife rejoices her husband through reverence and he walks in his integrity.
precepts.point: Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord: the same way you submit to Christ and the Most High, not less and not below it. Scripture defines marriage by function, not feelings. Traditions carry meaning, but they do not replace the original design. Function first, and through aging together the feelings do what they do.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

precepts.why:
“A virtuous woman rejoiceth her husband, and he shall fulfil the years of his life in peace.” The Bible calls for peace in the marriage: not war, not strife, not enmity, not division, not variance.

This is how the trouble in the flesh of 1 Corinthians 7:28 is handled. The wife focuses on rejoicing her husband through reverence, and then he stands in his integrity, because there is peace in the household. Peace, not passion. Peace, not feelings.

That reverence is what Ephesians 5:33 asks: “the wife see that she reverence her husband.” Reverence is beyond respect. It is a profound, heartfelt attitude of awe, that manifests as obedience and submission. It cannot be done as a job description; it has to come from the heart, and if a sister does not have that spirit she has to pray for it. When it comes from genuine respect and a desire to please the Lord, she will not be derelict in her duties, and the house has peace.

precepts.text: My son, keep the flower of thine age sound, and give not thy strength to strangers. When thou hast gotten a fruitful possession, sow it with thine own seed, trusting in the goodness of thy stock; so thy race shall be magnified, having the confidence of their good descent. A brother who gets money and marries a heathen gives his strength to strangers; sow among your own people and your race is magnified.
precepts.point: Thou shalt not sow thy vineyard with divers seeds, lest the fruit of thy seed and the fruit of thy vineyard be defiled. This is more than agriculture: when we deal with other nations, the children brought forth are defiled and confused, as in the book of Nehemiah.

note.label: A Tree Bearing No Fruits

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not sow thy vineyard with divers seeds: lest the fruit of thy seed which thou hast sown, and the fruit of thy vineyard, be defiled.” Reading that, we might think only of agriculture or farming, but it is talking about much more than that, and Sirach 26 shows what.

“My son, keep the flower of thine age sound; and give not thy strength to strangers.” The strangers are the heathen, the other nations. Then it explains how you give your strength to them: “When thou hast gotten a fruitful possession through all the field, sow it with thine own seed.” A fruitful possession means you have a position, you have money, you are rich. Sow it with your own seed means sow it with your own people. You got money? Don't be going and marrying no damn white woman. What a lot of brothers do today, the first thing when they get money, is go marry a heathen. When you marry the heathen when you are rich, you are giving your strength unto strangers.

Instead, deal with your own people: start a family with the woman God created for you, “trusting in the goodness of thy stock.” Your stock is your nationality, your race, your people. You are a son of God; why would you want to go deal with other nations?

“So thy race which thou leavest shall be magnified, having the confidence of their good descent.” When you marry your sisters and bring forth children among your people, your children and your race are magnified. Good descent means your children are not confused about what their nationality is, because you did not sow your seed among all different kinds of heathen women, as our forefathers did in the book of Nehemiah.

That is the law of Deuteronomy 22:9. When we go and deal with other nations, the fruit of the vineyard is defiled: the children brought forth, the descendants, are defiled and confused.

precepts.text: He shall save his people from their sins.
precepts.point: Keep the flower of thine age sound, give not thy strength to strangers, and sow thine own seed, that thy race may be magnified.

note.label: 2025 Recap: Different Times, Same Truth

precepts.why:
A well-respected black theologian, preaching before white people all over the place, taught that race is a social construct and not a biblical concept. False. The Bible is the family tree; Genesis 10 is the table of nations. Sirach says: “My son, keep the flower of thine age sound; and give not thy strength to strangers”: keep your seed, your nobility, your race, and don’t pollute it with other nations. “When thou hast gotten a fruitful possession through all the field”, find your wife, “sow it with thine own seed, trusting in the goodness of thy stock.” Seed and race are the same thing. “So thy race which thou leavest shall be magnified, having the confidence of their good descent.” So what is he talking about? These pastors don’t know the Bible, and he never opened it once.

Matthew shows who Christ came for: “And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.” His people. You go to somebody’s house and they say, that’s his people: that means his family, his kinfolk. The Bible was written by black people, and kindred and kinfolk are all in it.

Christ came to save his own race. He never came for any other race or nation. That is why the old family Bibles had the whole lineage written in them.

Yes, we all come from Adam, but Ezra makes the difference: of Adam come we all, “And the people also whom thou hast chosen.” As for the other people which also come of Adam, “thou hast said that they are nothing.” God chose a people out of Adam, and those are the people Christ came to save from their sins. Time is up on the Christian church.

precepts.text: Let every one of you so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband.
precepts.point: Reverence is deep respect laced with awe; its opposite is contempt.

note.label: Transforming From Immorality To Beautiful Civility Returning Our Kingdom To An Organized Nation Pt 3

precepts.why:
“A woman that honoureth her husband shall be judged wise of all; but she that dishonoureth him in her pride shall be counted ungodly of all.” This is your wisdom, sisters: honor the husband. Dishonoring him in pride sounds like, damn, I got to be up under a man? Nah, I got a direct line to Jesus. And “an honest woman will reverence her husband.”

Look up reverence and meditate on it; it goes beyond respect. It is a feeling or attitude of deep respect tinged with awe, veneration. Your man is on a pedestal; he walks in the house and everything gets still to welcome him home. Women understand it, because they do it when they go to work. And there is an outward manifestation: actions that demonstrate it, not, you know I had a hard day, you know what my boss said. If the definition is hard, read the opposite and don’t do that: contempt. If there is a tinge of contempt in your spirit toward your husband, that is what Sirach calls ungodly. We have seen marriages in the congregation where the wife showed nothing but contempt.

Paul uses the same word: “Nevertheless let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband.” The husband gives first. He loves his wife as himself; she is his comfort, she charges his batteries, and he will put his life on the line for her. When you love your wife, your family and your nation, you will go to war to protect it. Any man who lets somebody run over his family is a damn fool.

And the wife reverences her husband. This is how we lost that honor and reverence: the kingdom of heaven suffered violence, and our women were taken from us. The Willie Lynch letter said to break the female until she submits completely to the slaveholder’s will, with no glimmer of honor left for her husband, so she would train her children to labor. That is why we see so much contempt now. Returning our kingdom to order means the husband loving as Christ loved and the wife reverencing her husband again.

precepts.text: If thy daughter be shameless, keep her in straitly, lest she abuse herself through overmuch liberty.
precepts.point: The lesson stands for every generation: keep watch over the daughters. Have a care of their body; do not give overmuch liberty; the father wakes for the daughter and the care for her takes away sleep. Everything the children do should have supervision, especially in this age.

note.label: Genesis 34: Dinah and the Zeal of Simeon and Levi

precepts.why:
“If thy daughter be shameless, keep her in straitly, lest she abuse herself through overmuch liberty.”

Dinah went out to see the daughters of the land without supervision, and Shechem took her and defiled her. Do not give overmuch liberty. Keep the daughters in straitly; everything the children do should have supervision, especially in this age.

precepts.text: A married woman is a tower against death to her husband; that is what Michal was to David that night.
precepts.point: Note Saul's words: why hast thou sent away mine enemy? Saul and David were brothers, both Israel, Benjamin and Judah; Saul made his brother his enemy, and David loved him anyway. That is the understanding of Christ's words on loving your enemy: David exemplified it with Saul.

note.label: 1 Samuel 19: A Faithful Friend Is a Strong Defence

precepts.why:
“An harlot shall be accounted as spittle; but a married woman is a tower against death to her husband.” That is what Michal was to David that night.

Saul “sent messengers unto David’s house, to watch him, and to slay him in the morning.” Having tried to turn his son against David, he now leans on his daughter, David's own wife. But Michal warned him: “If thou save not thy life to night, to morrow thou shalt be slain.” She “let David down through a window: and he went, and fled, and escaped.”

She laid an image in the bed with “a pillow of goats’ hair for his bolster”, and told the messengers, “He is sick.” Saul said, “Bring him up to me in the bed, that I may slay him”, and they found the image. Michal covered herself, saying David threatened her, “Let me go; why should I kill thee?”, but she was looking out for her husband.

At this time Michal was a righteous example, a ride or die. She turns sour some chapters down the line, but here she saved his life.

precepts.text: Such a wife is priceless, a shamefaced and faithful woman.
precepts.point: He that covers a transgression seeks love, but he that repeats a matter separates very friends. Covering sin like Ananias and Sapphira, who conspired to lie to the apostles, is condemned.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“A gift is as a precious stone in the eyes of him that hath it: whithersoever it turneth, it prospereth.” A well-instructed wife is one of these gifts: “A silent and loving woman is a gift of the Lord; and there is nothing so much worth as a mind well instructed.”

A silent and loving woman does not mean one who never talks. It means a shamefaced sister who is not a chest bumper, a faithful woman whose continent mind cannot be valued. Such a wife is priceless.

precepts.text: Harlots try to entice with the eyes, which is why the Most High wants our sisters to be shame-faced rather than painting the eyes for enticement.
precepts.point: A voice of a multitude at ease was with her, and Sabeans and drunkards were brought from the wilderness who put bracelets on her hands and crowns on her head; being old in adulteries, the nations went in unto her as men go in unto a harlot.

note.label: Ezekiel 23: Aholah and Aholibah, the Two Harlot Sisters

precepts.why:
For the men she sent for from far, she “paintedst thy eyes, and deckedst thyself with ornaments”. “The whoredom of a woman may be known in her haughty looks and eyelids.” Harlots try to entice with the eyes. That is why she painted them.

She washed herself, painted her eyes, decked herself, and sat “upon a stately bed, and a table prepared before it, whereupon thou hast set mine incense and mine oil.” Like an adulteress fixing herself up in her husband's house with his own things to lie with another man, we prepared the bed with the Most High's own incense and oil for the nations. Being old in adulteries, the nations went in unto her “as they go in unto a woman that playeth the harlot”.

This is why the Most High wants our sisters to be shame-faced, not painting the eyes for enticement. Painted eyes and haughty looks are the mark of the whoredom of a woman, and they are the mark of Aholah and Aholibah, the lewd women.

note.label: Passover: a Celebration of Deliverance From Oppression

precepts.why:
This is what the Bishop is warning about, the reproach that is coming on the heritage. “There be three things that mine heart feareth; and for the fourth I was sore afraid”, sore afraid meaning very afraid.

“The slander of a city”: have we not been slandered, have not lies been coming up about us? “The gathering together of an unruly multitude”: that other five dollar Indian is trying to do that, gathering an unruly multitude with lies. “And a false accusation”: have we not had false accusations put against us?

“All these are worse than death.” It is worse than dying, because you can’t sleep, you can’t move, you can’t think, with so many people ready to attack you at once with slander, false accusation and lies.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

precepts.why:
He wasn’t crap, and guess who wasn’t crap either: she wasn’t crap either. He’s a piece of doodoo and she’s a big piece of doodoo too. That’s how it is, and it’s Bible; God said it, it wasn’t made up. “A wicked woman is given as a portion to a wicked man”: two pieces of doodoo collide. You’re a misogynist, you hate women? No; I just don’t kiss women’s behind.

We’re glad brothers and sisters are in here trying to get their lives right, but there’s always that one, she or he, waiting: who can I burn, who can I take advantage of. There are people in here that ain’t no good, looking to burn you.

note.label: THE REBIRTH OF GOD’S NATION ON THE EARTH

precepts.why:
These are the scriptures that tell what she brings to his bones. “The grace of a wife delighteth her husband”: a wife, not a jump-off, not a hoe. “And her discretion will fatten his bones”: she is not stupid. He lights up, he’s happy; she is adding years to his life. That is what you should be thinking about when you look for a wife. You come to her father and ask for her hand, and the father checks you all the way out; if he finds you worthy, you had better take care of her.

“A silent and loving woman is a gift of the Lord.” She is not going to be silent if the bills aren’t paid, or if you are battling four or five women. She may be tricked into thinking she is all right, but inside she is mad as hell. You can’t treat her like garbage.

“And there is nothing so much worth as a mind well instructed.” Ponder that. When you see married men do great things, what do other men say? He must have a good woman behind him: she fattens his bones. Her daddy taught her well, and the people she came up around taught her well. That is what you want by your side, brothers, a wife to grow aged together with.

points: A silent and loving woman is a gift of the Lord; and there is nothing so much worth as a mind well instructed. That is another example to show you that the silence does not always exclusively mean just be quiet. It talks about a mind well instructed, meaning that your behaviours are what matter behind that.

You cannot be a silent loving woman if your mind is not well instructed. That is you that has to learn. That is you that has to study those things, especially the way this world is set up. You have to seek out the book and meditate on the things you need to improve in. That is why we had to rein in some of the Titus subjects some years back, because you were out here teaching all this women's empowerment stuff veiled as scriptures. And we said no — Titus 2 says teach them how to love their husbands, love their children, guide the house. You were more focused on your best friend, sisterhood, than you were about the foundational things that actually make you a strong believing woman in the scriptures.

Discreet means prudent and discerning: you are able to speak and act with sound judgment. You learn not to be sarcastic, not to be questioning, not to be disrespectful. Silent goes into quiet and peaceable: you are not always arguing, you do not want to quarrel, you are not ruled by the need to say something. It does not mean mute — now if your husband likes mute, adapt to him. Loving means showing affection, goodwill and devoted care to your husband, however he likes to be cared for. You have got to learn that, not the way you think. Well instructed means your mind and your spirit is governed by those principles, by those commandments. Shamefaced: having a proper sense of shame, not brazen — you are not shamefaced when you start talking all extra and aggressive. Faithful means trustworthy, loyal, dependable to him. Continent goes into being self-disciplined, self-controlled and restrained, especially in your appetites, your passions and your conduct. And orderly: well-arranged and disciplined, including the ordering of the house. It is a very rare man that is all right with a messy home. Most men are built for order. That is why we like to see the schools a certain way, we like to see our homes a certain way.
